instructions: Cut the rack of ribs apart between the bones so you have individual ribs. If the butcher hasn't already, cut them in half crosswise.
Put the ribs in a large pot and cover with cold water. Add 1/2 tsp of the salt. Bring to a boil over high heat and boil for 5 minutes, until grey scum rises to the top.
Drain the ribs into a colander and rinse them well under cold water. Rinse out the pot too.

Mince the shallot and the garlic. In a large bowl, mix them with 1/2 tbsp of the fish sauce, 1/2 tbsp of the sugar, the oil and 1/4 tsp of the pepper. Add the ribs and toss to coat. Leave them for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and put it on to cook according to the package. Slice the green onions. Slice the chilies thin and put them in a small bowl for the table.

Put the 2 tbsp remaining sugar in the clean pot, off the heat, and spread it flat. Set the pot over medium-low heat and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, swirling now and then, until the sugar melts and turns a deep amber. Don't walk away. It goes from amber to burnt fast.
Add the ribs and all the marinade. Stand back a little. It will spatter. Stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until the ribs are coated and the pink is mostly gone.
Pour in the coconut water, add the remaining 2 tbsp fish sauce and the last 1/4 tsp pepper, and bring to a boil. If the ribs aren't about half covered, add a splash of water.
Lower the heat to low, cover, and cook for 30 to 40 minutes, until the meat is tender and pulls easily from the bone. Skim off any foam from the top.
Uncover and raise the heat to medium-high. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick and sticky and coats the ribs.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Sprinkle with the green onions. Serve with the rice and put the sliced chilies on the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: The sources agree on parboiling the ribs, marinating briefly with fish sauce and aromatics, then braising in a sugar caramel with coconut water until glazed. They differ on the liquid (Coco Rico, coconut water or plain water), the extras (oyster sauce and Sriracha in Savour the Pho, bouillon and char siu sauce in Noms by Nancy) and the time (30 to 40 minutes covered). I followed the lead, left out the MSG and chilies in the pot so the base stays mild, and moved the chilies to the table. The two other sources show no ratings.
